name: Belle-Isle Pidgin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct pidgin; Glottolog lists no descriptive references at all.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page bell1264 (HTML + JSON) — classification Pidgin > French-based pidgin; single MED = Dorais 1996, med_type wordlist_or_less; links to Wikidata Q6467589 and en.wikipedia 'Labrador Inuit Pidgin French'.
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic record only. Note: says Glottolog lists no refs, but Glottolog 5.3 and the held hh.bib both carry Dorais 1996 (glottolog_ref_id 23292, hhtype minimal) and Bakker 1991 (hhtype overview) under 'Belle-Isle Pidgin' / 'Inuit-French Jargon'.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter. 1991. Trade languages in the Strait of Belle Isle. Journal of the Atlantic Provinces Linguistic Association 13: 1-19 (Inuit French Jargon section pp. 7-10).
sources.note: Nothing. The pidgin is documented only through five or six phrases copied from 18th-century written records (Fornel 1743 'tout camara troquo balena, non charraco'; Drachart 1765 'tout camerade, oui hu'; Cugnet 1743 'Bons camaras, Capitaine Le Cour'), plus a score of words quoted from Cranz 1820; no phonology, no stress, no accent marks. Only phonological remark (p. 8): 'tout is probably Spanish tu... (or French tu adapted to Inuktitut phonology)'.
